name: block-visibility
notes: Adapter-authoring probe 2026-09-08: official WordPress.org Block Visibility 3.7.1 (SHA-256 1b889bb9f5c650fd89bc968f26a4acf01355cc58736eabc8da63cab213710a9a), measured live on WordPress 7.1. Persistent surface: one option (block_visibility_settings), one post type (visibility_preset) with four registered meta keys, and the blockVisibility block attribute. No taxonomy, custom table, transient, cron event, user meta, shortcode or widget.

The option is fully portable and withholds nothing: visibility_controls is sixteen boolean toggles, disabled_blocks is a list of BLOCK NAMES rather than ids, and plugin_settings holds scalars plus role slugs. It is measured ABSENT on a fresh install until the first save, and this capsule deliberately does NOT complete that absence from the plugin's registered defaults: unlike Speculative Loading, Block Visibility builds its defaults inside register_settings() and publishes them only through register_setting() on rest_api_init/admin_init, neither of which a capture process fires, so there is no in-process way to read them from the plugin itself. An absent row therefore captures as absence and the disposition records it as an unsupported surface rather than substituting a hardcoded copy.

WHY THE BLOCK ATTRIBUTE REMAINS UNSUPPORTED. The plugin's primary surface is a block attribute injected into EVERY registered block, carrying entity ids at conditionally-typed nested paths. block_attrs binds one top-level attribute key per EXACT block name over a value vocabulary the engine closes at {int,int[]} ('any other shape needs engine support before it can be declared', AttributeGrammar). Neither the any-block reach nor the nested conditional paths are expressible today, so the certified boundary deliberately excludes this attribute while still migrating the settings and entity-free preset storage.

WHY IT REFUSES RATHER THAN CAPTURING. Undeclared, those ids reach canonical state verbatim and land on a target pointing at unrelated entities, and lint does NOT catch it: unregistered_block_attr fires on attributes named id/ids/ref or ending in Id/Ids holding a NUMERIC value, while blockVisibility is an object. Every block that can carry it therefore declares it `unsupported`, a reviewed blocking boundary that fires only when a block actually holds the attribute -- ordinary content capture is untouched. The same structure recurs in the visibility_preset meta key control_sets, which the interpreter admits only when every control in it is on a reviewed reference-free ALLOWLIST. That direction is deliberate: a denylist of reference-bearing field names cannot stay complete against this plugin -- WooCommerce keeps its product id in a rule's subField rather than its value (woocommerce/helper-functions.php:376-383) and userRole carries restrictedUsers user ids in one of its modes (user-role.php:125-156), so an unreviewed or newly added control refuses instead of being captured. tools/engine-gaps.json records the demand as any_block_structured_attribute_reference_paths.

WHY THE CORE RULES ARE RESTATED HERE. ContentAttributeRuleResolver::block_attr_rules() replaces a block's whole rule LIST per block name, last pin wins (agent/src/Grammar/ContentAttributeRuleResolver.php:16-23) -- it is not a per-path merge. Declaring only `blockVisibility` on a block the platform core manifest also declares would therefore DELETE core's rules for it, and core declares 21 of these blocks: core/image's post ref, core/gallery's ids, core/block's reusable-block ref, core/avatar's user ref, the navigation refs, and eighteen URL tokenizers. That would turn this capsule into a cause of exactly the silent id leakage it exists to prevent. Each overlapping entry therefore restates core's rules verbatim and appends its own, the complete-superset shape The Events Calendar's core/legacy-widget codec already uses; tests/offline/regress_package_contract.php asserts the superset per block, so a core rule added later fails this capsule's gate instead of being silently dropped. core/legacy-widget is deliberately NOT declared at all: The Events Calendar owns it with a whole-block codec, and any declaration here would clobber that codec whenever this capsule sorts later in the pin list.
